claim: On host nativestack-5975wx-20260925 on 2026-09-29 and 2026-09-30, socraticode 1.16.0 (tag v1.16.0, annotated tag object a50f72c5b79dcb8f69ac9bc68b21fe744d82d45b, commit 3d3a4a4d427cb0f29de4f5dd1360da52896f62df, released 2026-09-28T12:19:47Z) was qualified as a candidate for the linux-x86_64 pin and installed in an unreferenced prefix; the pin stays 1.15.0 and nothing was cut over. The npm tarball https://registry.npmjs.org/socraticode/-/socraticode-1.16.0.tgz (1,065,187 bytes, published 2026-09-28T12:23:47.213Z) had sha256 3cb602cf2f50f863ef79dde56923d65b7ce840e2cc26070efa41743d2b4aaafe, sha512 equal to npm dist.integrity sha512-Lsei32zdHES3fCIRROn7kb1FY7sia0Oe2ZZMRUShZy8AytaqUB2F7/fF2+2dDLNNZxNAURP2Sb0doSpHv8JbMA== and sha1 equal to dist.shasum 44a18caf99a4f4f466e3d618860143dec51bfd71. Its registry gitHead 3e3b4b3d7bbe29b8cf5908bca3f06ef416bff4a3 is the tag commit's parent: the two commits differ only in 10 release-bookkeeping files and in no line of src/, the tarball's 16 non-dist files are byte-identical to the tag tree, and its 223 dist files are byte-identical to an npm run build of the tag. The upstream suite passed at the tag: in a clean clone at 3d3a4a4d with Node v24.21.0 (npm 11.19.0), npm ci exited 0 (425 packages, 0 vulnerabilities, package-lock.json unchanged), npm run test:unit exited 0 (107 of 107 files, 2,517 of 2,517 tests passed), npm run check:release-versions exited 0 ('release manifests match 1.16.0'), npx biome check src/ tests/ exited 0 (184 files, no fixes), npx tsc --noEmit exited 0, and ci.yml's four Qdrant-backed regressions with REQUIRE_QDRANT=1 against a disposable Qdrant 1.19.1 exited 0 (4 files, 12 of 12 tests); an independent verifier re-ran all six commands from a fresh clone with the same results. On a project-local npm install --before=2026-09-28T12:30:00Z resolution of the tag with the lockfile removed, the recipe's cutoff, npm run test:unit exited 0 (107 of 107 files, 2,517 of 2,517 tests) and npx tsc --noEmit exited 0. Between v1.15.0 and v1.16.0 the 26 MCP tool registrations, the package.json dependencies, INDEX_FORMAT_VERSION 2, SCHEMA_VERSION 1 and the lock-directory format are unchanged, and SOCRATICODE_WATCHER still defaults to auto; the new Git-triggered refresh runs only when it is set to git, which nothing in this repository does. The host's tools/socraticode-1.16.0 prefix holds the same 178 package versions as the evaluated recipe tree, and no running process named it at 2026-09-30T00:28:23Z, when 7 processes ran the 1.15.0 prefix.
limitations: Not cut over, and nothing in the claim rests on a cutover. No client configuration references tools/socraticode-1.16.0 yet (coordinator observation; the Claude Code and Codex user configurations are repointed only after the Gate A owner approves), and no production client (mcporter, Claude Code or Codex) called a 1.16.0 server, so unlike the 1.15.0 receipt there is no native-client or production-service evidence for 1.16.0; no MCP initialize, tools/list or codebase_health call was made against the installed 1.16.0 prefix either. The Linux pin in adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json and manifests/stack.json therefore stays 1.15.0 in the change that adds this receipt, as it stayed at 1.14.0 while the 1.15.0 cutover was deferred (docs/decisions/2026-09-25-workstation-sota-refresh.md). Moving the pin would itself start a cutover: adoption/update.md re-runs the bootstrap after a pin change, which reinstalls into tools/socraticode-1.16.0 without --before and repoints bin/socraticode, and tools/adoption/render_config.py and the landscape sweep's scratch Codex homes render the pinned prefix into any configuration rendered from main. The installed prefix makes such a re-render a silent cutover, not a visible failure. The pin moves at the cutover, after Gate A's window W closes and no earlier than 2026-10-05T12:23Z unless the user waives the cooldown; an independent review of the branch that moves it found this on 2026-09-30, and that branch is kept unmerged.

Cooldown not served and not waived. docs/decisions/2026-09-25-workstation-sota-refresh.md held 1.15.0's cutover for a 7-day cooldown for a release that is not a security fix (2026-10-01T11:01Z, seven days after its npm publish), which the user waived on 2026-09-27. No recorded decision applies or waives that gate for 1.16.0; by the same rule its earliest cutover is 2026-10-05T12:23Z. v1.16.0 carries upstream's dependency-security follow-up (#192, #193), and npm ci's audit of the lockfile tree, dev dependencies included, reported 0 vulnerabilities at v1.16.0 against 3 moderate at v1.15.0; the advisories were not reviewed, so whether 1.16.0 counts as a security fix is not established here.

Evidence classes differ by part. The upstream suite is the unchanged upstream test code at the tag, run twice (data.upstream_suite, with its deviations). The --before re-run is the same upstream test code on another dependency tree (data.dependency_tree.before_tree_suite). The tarball content comparison, the dependency-tree comparisons and the host-prefix comparison are local integration checks. Upstream's GitHub check runs at the tag commit (data.upstream_ci) are upstream platform records, not execution on this host. The host install is the coordinator's native operation, and that no client configuration references the prefix is the coordinator's reported observation. One deliberately failing control was run on 2026-09-30 at the tag: with REQUIRE_QDRANT=1 and no Qdrant reachable (QDRANT_URL and QDRANT_PORT on a closed loopback port), tests/integration/partial-upsert-skip.test.ts exited 1 with 'REQUIRE_QDRANT=1 but Qdrant is not reachable. This regression must fail rather than skip', so the Qdrant-backed regressions cannot pass by skipping. No failing control was run for the unit suite itself; its weight rests on upstream's own assertions and on 107 run files equal to the tracked tests/unit count.

The tested trees differ from the installed tree. The upstream suite and the Qdrant regressions ran on upstream's package-lock.json tree, while the recipe is a global install with --ignore-scripts and --before=2026-09-28T12:30:00Z, the earliest cutoff tried after the npm publish; the package ships no shrinkwrap. That tree holds 18 production packages at another version than the lockfile (for example @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.1 against 1.30.0, openai 6.49.0 against 6.48.0, @lumis-sh/wasm-eex 0.26.2 against 0.26.1, jose 6.2.12 against 6.2.3 and typescript 7.0.2 against 5.9.3) plus typescript's linux-x64 binary. The --before re-run of the unit suite and tsc used a project-local resolution at the same cutoff, which adds devDependencies and ran lifecycle scripts; it holds every package version of the recipe tree except typescript 7.0.2 and its binary, because upstream's devDependencies hold typescript at ^5.7.3 (5.9.3). typescript enters the recipe tree only as the auto-installed peer of @qdrant/js-client-rest 1.18.0, no file in socraticode's dist or the client's dist imports it, and the production 1.15.0 prefix carries the same typescript 7.0.2. The four Qdrant-backed regressions were not re-run on a --before tree. Later cutoffs drift further (at 2026-09-29T23:00:00Z: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.31.0, @lumis-sh/wasm-eex and wasm-heex 0.26.3, hono 4.13.11). adoption/bootstrap-linux.sh install_npm passes no --before, so a bootstrap install can resolve yet another tree.

Not run on this host: git-refresh-integration, the CI job for the headline feature (it needs Docker and Ollama with nomic-embed-text, neither is on this host's PATH, and its two test files skip themselves without Docker, so running them would report only skips); git-refresh-windows on windows-latest (its three test files ran on Linux instead); node-floor-consumer-install on Node 18.17.0; the packaged-consumer step of node-26-consumer-qdrant; rust-graph-vs-cargo; npm run test:integration and npm run test:e2e. On this host the live Git-refresh path (real git, embeddings, Qdrant, two MCP processes) is covered only by unit tests, and it stays dormant unless SOCRATICODE_WATCHER is set to git. Upstream's own check runs at the tag commit (data.upstream_ci: 13 check runs, all successful) cover the CI jobs in that list; that is upstream's record, not a run here. No upstream workflow runs npm run test:integration or npm run test:e2e: CI runs 7 of the 18 tests/integration files (the four Qdrant-backed regressions, the two git-refresh integration files and rust-graph-vs-cargo), so the other 11 integration files and the e2e file ran neither upstream nor here.

The runs deviate from upstream CI. Node v24.21.0 is outside the CI unit matrix (18/20/22/26) and differs from the Qdrant job's Node 26. Qdrant 1.19.1 ran as a native binary on a loopback port with scratch storage instead of the qdrant/qdrant:v1.17.0 service container. npm run build ran before the regressions, as ci.yml:149 does, although no test reads dist/ (the 1.15.0 run skipped it). HOME and the npm cache pointed into scratch, and 52 service and configuration variable names were unset. Commands ran through rtk proxy with output redirected to logs. npm ci warned that 19 packages have install scripts not yet covered by allowScripts; this was not reviewed here.

Side effects and a failed attempt on the shared host. The scout's runs kept the default TMPDIR, so the upstream tests wrote 77 lock files holding dead test PIDs into the shared socraticode lock directory that production servers use; the verifier's re-run used a private TMPDIR and wrote none there, and the 77 entries were later removed by an actor this record does not identify. Two already-running 1.15.0 MCP servers exited during the scout's window; no link to the runs was found and the cause is not established. A first supplementary run of the three Git-refresh unit files, with TMPDIR inside scratch, failed 2 of 25 tests with 'listen EINVAL' because the tsx IPC socket path reached 130 characters, over the 107 usable bytes of sun_path; the same files passed under the default TMPDIR and inside the 107-file run, so it is not an upstream failure.

The landscape ledger does not move: catalogs/landscape/foundation.json keeps the winner pin socraticode 1.14.0 from the sealed 2026-09-22 layer-verdict packets. A host receipt recorded at 1.16.0 therefore matches no winner pin; scripts/host_receipts.py record refuses it unless --allow-unbound-version is passed, and it stays unbound until a new verdict wave re-records the layer.

Linux x86_64 only: adoption/pins-macos-arm64.json keeps socraticode 1.14.0 and the Linux pin stays 1.15.0 until the cutover, so the Mac lags the Linux pin by one minor version now and by two once the pin moves. The npm tarball is platform-independent, but a Mac needs its own acceptance, and nothing here is macOS evidence.

Upstream reports rule out only what is reported. The check at 2026-09-30T00:20Z (data.upstream_state) found no newer release, main identical to v1.16.0, and one open pull request (#195, after the closed, unmerged #194) about codebase_health failing against a healthy Qdrant on a distribution-built Node 24.21.0 whose bundled undici handler has no onError. That pull request lists the official Node 24.21.0 build (undici 7.29.1) as working; this host's Node reports undici 7.29.1 and the Qdrant regressions passed on it, and src/services/qdrant-client-compat.ts is identical at v1.15.0 and v1.16.0, so the report is not a 1.16.0 change.
